claim_text: In two studies of people with sleep problems (139 and 64 participants), nighttime sleep-related worry was consistently associated with sleep impairment. Trait rumination and trait worry were not associated with sleep impairment in Study 1.
limitations: Evidence concerns people with sleep problems. It does not establish that everyone overthinks more at night.
reviewer_notes: Supported by S01 abstract; retain population and association qualifiers.

claim_text: In a sample of 507 undergraduates, bedtime repetitive negative thinking moderated the relationship between perceived stress and insomnia severity. The pattern differed between participants above and below the insomnia threshold.
limitations: Observational study in undergraduates. The relationship does not establish causation or universal applicability.
reviewer_notes: Supported by S02 abstract; do not present as universal causal law.

claim_text: A systematic review included 12 articles in its synthesis, identified nine distinct theoretical models of insomnia, and extracted 20 cognitive factors and processes (39 when sub-factors were counted).
limitations: This review maps theoretical models; it does not mean every person with insomnia experiences all identified cognitive factors.
reviewer_notes: Corrected after checking PubMed and open-access full bibliographic record. 12 refers to included articles, not 12 models.

claim_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis covering 154 studies and 5,717 participants found that experimental sleep loss reduced positive affect and increased anxiety symptoms. Findings for negative affect were mixed.
limitations: This evidence concerns effects of sleep loss on emotion. It does not prove that sleep loss causes nighttime overthinking.
reviewer_notes: Preserve the mixed-results qualification for negative affect.

claim_text: For adults with chronic insomnia disorder, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine strongly recommends multicomponent cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I); sleep hygiene alone is not recommended as a standalone treatment.
limitations: The recommendation concerns adults with chronic insomnia disorder. It is not individualized medical advice.

claim_text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 randomized trials found CBT-I had moderate-to-large effects on worry (Hedges g approximately -0.41 to -0.71), while its effect on rumination was small and not reliable (g approximately -0.13).
limitations: Evidence base is limited and developing. Do not claim CBT-I eliminates all forms of overthinking.
